representation: MODRISS JSON DSL mapped to SPEM 2.0

roleDefinitions.name: Sponsor
responsibilities: Authorizes investment and accepts pursue, redirect, stop, and final closure decisions

roleDefinitions.name: Product Owner
responsibilities: Owns product outcomes, priority, release scope, and acceptance decisions

roleDefinitions.name: Delivery Lead
responsibilities: Maintains the integrated process run, dependency board, risks, cadence, and impediment escalation

roleDefinitions.name: Business Modeler
responsibilities: Leads CIM discovery and domain-model increments

roleDefinitions.name: Requirements Engineer
responsibilities: Maintains requirements, acceptance criteria, and change impact evidence

roleDefinitions.name: Domain Expert
responsibilities: Validates business language, rules, and operational fit

roleDefinitions.name: Solution Architect
responsibilities: Leads PIM architecture, contracts, integration, and cross-level decisions

roleDefinitions.name: Cloud Platform Engineer
responsibilities: Leads AWS PSM, generation, environments, and platform automation

roleDefinitions.name: Quality Engineer
responsibilities: Owns verification strategy, evidence quality, and quality risks

roleDefinitions.name: Security Engineer
responsibilities: Owns security, privacy, threat, and exception evidence

roleDefinitions.name: Release Engineer
responsibilities: Owns release candidates, promotion, rollback, and deployment records

roleDefinitions.name: Service Owner
responsibilities: Accepts operational readiness, SLOs, support ownership, and service outcomes

roleDefinitions.name: Process Reviewer
responsibilities: Reviews gates, evidence, decisions, and process improvement

roleDefinitions.name: Method Engineer
responsibilities: Tailors the development process and maintains its alignment with the modeling framework as metamodels change

roleDefinitions.name: FinOps and Cost Analyst
responsibilities: Owns cost hypotheses, budgets, allocation, anomaly thresholds, forecasts, and unit economics

roleDefinitions.name: Records and Data Steward
responsibilities: Owns retention, export, deletion, disposition evidence, and records custody through closure

taskDefinitions.name: Define product outcomes and success measures
taskDefinitions.purpose: Define product outcomes and success measures
steps: State the user or mission problem and desired outcomes.
Define measurable product, operational, security, quality, and cost/value outcomes.
Record assumptions, constraints, non-goals, expected lifetime, exit conditions, and the first release hypothesis.
exitCriteria: Outcome measures and non-goals are accepted by stakeholders
validationRules: Every initial scope item is connected to an outcome or mandatory constraint
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Define product outcomes and success measures decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Establish the initial release and increment hypothesis
taskDefinitions.purpose: Establish the initial release and increment hypothesis
steps: Identify the smallest useful vertical capability slice.
Define acceptance signals and the evidence needed to call it usable.
Record unresolved assumptions as owned decisions rather than hidden risks.
exitCriteria: Establish the initial release and increment hypothesis evidence is recorded
validationRules: The first slice crosses the required lifecycle boundary and has observable acceptance evidence
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Establish the initial release and increment hypothesis decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Assess feasibility and serverless suitability
taskDefinitions.purpose: Assess feasibility and serverless suitability
steps: Compare serverless, hybrid, and non-serverless alternatives against workload shape, latency, state, integration, availability, compliance, skills, operations, portability, and exit constraints.
Use bounded architecture experiments for material uncertainty and record provider assumptions separately from platform-independent intent.
Record the recommended direction, rejected alternatives, residual risks, and review triggers.
exitCriteria: Assess feasibility and serverless suitability evidence is recorded
validationRules: The recommendation compares credible alternatives rather than assuming serverless
Material uncertainty has an owner and an experiment or decision deadline
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Assess feasibility and serverless suitability decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Establish cost model and budget guardrails
taskDefinitions.purpose: Establish cost model and budget guardrails
steps: Model demand drivers and scenario ranges for requests, duration, memory, data transfer, storage, logs, workflows, and external services.
Define allocation tags, business unit-cost metrics, budget/forecast ranges, anomaly thresholds, and confidence assumptions.
Identify cost-sensitive architecture decisions and the runtime evidence needed to recalibrate estimates.
exitCriteria: Establish cost model and budget guardrails evidence is recorded
validationRules: The estimate states workload assumptions, range, confidence, owner, and review cadence
At least one business unit-cost measure links technology spend to product value
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Establish cost model and budget guardrails decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Authorize pursue, explore, redirect, or stop at G0
taskDefinitions.purpose: Authorize pursue, explore, redirect, or stop at G0
steps: Review the product value case, suitability recommendation, cost range, material risks, and proposed experiments.
Record one explicit G0 decision: pursue, explore, redirect, or stop.
For pursue or explore, record funding/time boundaries, decision owners, and conditions that trigger reconsideration.
exitCriteria: An authorized G0 decision and its conditions are recorded
validationRules: Silence or task completion is not authorization
A stop or redirect decision preserves the rationale and evidence
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Authorize pursue, explore, redirect, or stop at G0 decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Assess context and process-tailoring risks
taskDefinitions.purpose: Assess context and process-tailoring risks
steps: Assess criticality, regulatory obligations, novelty, uncertainty, team distribution, system size, and delivery cadence.
Select the required CIM, PIM, PSM, artifact, and lifecycle activities.
Record excluded, combined, or delegated activities with rationale and compensating evidence.
exitCriteria: Assess context and process-tailoring risks evidence is recorded
validationRules: Every tailoring decision names its context, consequence, owner, and review point
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Assess context and process-tailoring risks decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Define the tailored Definition of Ready and Done
taskDefinitions.purpose: Define the tailored Definition of Ready and Done
steps: Define entry and exit evidence for model slices, transformations, release candidates, operations, and retirement.
Define which findings are blocking, who may accept residual risk, and how time-bound risk acceptance works.
Publish the profile version used by the process run.
exitCriteria: Define the tailored Definition of Ready and Done evidence is recorded
validationRules: A task cannot be accepted solely because activity occurred; required evidence and gate criteria are explicit
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Define the tailored Definition of Ready and Done decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Define team ownership and interfaces
taskDefinitions.purpose: Define team ownership and interfaces
steps: Partition work by bounded capability, service, platform concern, or lifecycle responsibility.
Assign model ownership, repository ownership, decision rights, and backup owners.
Define interface contracts and the shared dependency board.
exitCriteria: Define team ownership and interfaces evidence is recorded
validationRules: Every owned model scope has one accountable owner and a named integration path
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Define team ownership and interfaces decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Set coordination cadence and escalation paths
taskDefinitions.purpose: Set coordination cadence and escalation paths
steps: Set local team syncs, cross-team integration reviews, increment reviews, release reviews, and retrospectives.
Define escalation thresholds for aging dependencies, blocking findings, and conflicting model ownership.
Define how concurrent model edits are merged, reviewed, and reconciled.
exitCriteria: Set coordination cadence and escalation paths evidence is recorded
validationRules: Coordination events produce decisions, dependency status, and evidence links
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Set coordination cadence and escalation paths decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Define quality and security control objectives
taskDefinitions.purpose: Define quality and security control objectives
steps: Identify privacy, threat, compliance, resilience, performance, accessibility, audit, cost, and records obligations.
Map control objectives to model evidence, generated artifact evidence, and explicit human decisions.
Set severity and blocking policies.
exitCriteria: Define quality and security control objectives evidence is recorded
validationRules: Critical controls have an accountable owner and verification evidence path
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Define quality and security control objectives decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Define operational and release strategy
taskDefinitions.purpose: Define operational and release strategy
steps: Define environments, support ownership, SLO hypotheses, observability expectations, cost signals, rollback posture, and release cadence.

Define the Kanban service-delivery system: board states and start/finish points, WIP controls, classes of service, service-level expectations, capacity allocation, replenishment and review cadences, and expedite/reconciliation policy.
Identify data migration, compatibility, records/retention, and progressive-delivery constraints and record the initial release decision policy.
exitCriteria: Define operational and release strategy evidence is recorded
validationRules: The release strategy names promotion, rollback, and post-deployment validation evidence
The operational policy prevents unknown future maintenance demand from being represented as pre-scheduled tasks
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Define operational and release strategy decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Plan the vertical increment
taskDefinitions.purpose: Plan the vertical increment
steps: Select scope from the ordered product backlog.
Define outcome, acceptance criteria, dependencies, risks, cost hypothesis, and expected model/artifact evidence.
Assign scope items to owning teams and establish the increment ledger.
exitCriteria: Increment scope, owners, acceptance evidence, dependencies, and cost-sensitive assumptions are agreed
validationRules: The slice is small enough to inspect end-to-end and large enough to demonstrate a user or operational outcome
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Plan the vertical increment decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Run the CIM increment
taskDefinitions.purpose: Run the CIM increment
steps: Execute the CIM process for the selected capability slice.
Record semantic decisions, assumptions, trace links, readiness findings, and accepted CIM revision.
Return unresolved cross-team or product decisions to the integrated decision register.
exitCriteria: CIM gate evidence is accepted or explicitly reworked
validationRules: Assistant-applied model changes pass structural Ecore/EMF conformance; semantic validation remains an explicit user/model validation workflow
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Run the CIM increment decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Execute and inspect CIM-to-PIM transformation
taskDefinitions.purpose: Execute and inspect CIM-to-PIM transformation
steps: Pin the source CIM revision and transformation profile.
Run the transformation and inspect report, trace links, assumptions, and manual decisions.
Accept, reject, or route each material decision and record the target PIM revision.
exitCriteria: Execute and inspect CIM-to-PIM transformation evidence is recorded
validationRules: Every generated target scope item is traceable to a source or explicit transformation decision
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Execute and inspect CIM-to-PIM transformation decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Run the PIM increment
taskDefinitions.purpose: Run the PIM increment
steps: Execute the PIM process for the transformed slice.
Review contracts, data access, integration, policy, platform mapping, cost drivers, and operational assumptions.
Record accepted PIM revision and open platform decisions.
exitCriteria: PIM gate evidence is accepted or explicitly reworked
validationRules: Generated PIM is treated as scaffolding until the solution architect accepts material decisions
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Run the PIM increment decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Execute and inspect PIM-to-PSM transformation
taskDefinitions.purpose: Execute and inspect PIM-to-PSM transformation
steps: Pin the source PIM revision and AWS mapping profile.
Run the transformation and inspect resource mappings, assumptions, security implications, and trace links.
Record accepted target PSM revision or route mapping gaps back to PIM.
exitCriteria: Execute and inspect PIM-to-PSM transformation evidence is recorded
validationRules: Every deployable PIM scope item has an accepted AWS mapping or a documented exception
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Execute and inspect PIM-to-PSM transformation decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Run the PSM increment
taskDefinitions.purpose: Run the PSM increment
steps: Execute the AWS PSM process for the transformed slice.
Review resource relationships, IAM, networking, data, eventing, APIs, workflows, observability, quotas, allocation tags, and operational views.
Record accepted PSM revision and unresolved deployment risks.
exitCriteria: PSM gate evidence is accepted or explicitly reworked
validationRules: AWS platform choices are traceable to accepted PIM intent or explicit platform decisions
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Run the PSM increment decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Generate and fingerprint the artifact baseline
taskDefinitions.purpose: Generate and fingerprint the artifact baseline
steps: Pin PSM revision, generator version, templates, and environment profile.
Generate application, infrastructure, configuration, tests, and documentation artifacts.
Record the generation manifest and route structural gaps to PSM or generator ownership.
exitCriteria: Generate and fingerprint the artifact baseline evidence is recorded
validationRules: The generated baseline is reproducible from recorded inputs and contains no secret material
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Generate and fingerprint the artifact baseline decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Run artifact readiness and accept the increment
taskDefinitions.purpose: Run artifact readiness and accept the increment
steps: Execute the artifact deployment-readiness process for the generated candidate.
Review verification, security, cost, rollback, operational, and acceptance evidence.
Record increment outcome, open findings, deferred scope, and feedback loops for the next cycle.
exitCriteria: Increment is accepted, explicitly deferred, or returned through a named rework loop
validationRules: No blocking finding is silently closed; risk acceptance is explicit, owned, time-bound, and traceable
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Run artifact readiness and accept the increment decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Review the increment and adapt the way of working
taskDefinitions.purpose: Review the increment and adapt the way of working
steps: Compare outcome, effort, queue time, rework, trace, cost, dependency, and finding evidence with the increment hypothesis.
Identify useful practices, avoidable burden, missing guidance, and candidate reusable assets.
Update the method profile, improvement record, owners, and experiment/review dates; record a reasoned no-op when no change is justified.
exitCriteria: The increment retrospective has an owned improvement decision or a reasoned no-op
validationRules: A local workaround is not generalized without its context and evidence
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Review the increment and adapt the way of working decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Assemble the release candidate
taskDefinitions.purpose: Assemble the release candidate
steps: Select accepted increments and compatible model/artifact revisions.
Resolve cross-team dependency and compatibility checks.
Create the release record with exact inputs and promotion sequence.
exitCriteria: Assemble the release candidate evidence is recorded
validationRules: Every release scope item maps to an accepted increment and exact artifact identity
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Assemble the release candidate decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Review release evidence and go/no-go criteria
taskDefinitions.purpose: Review release evidence and go/no-go criteria
steps: Inspect readiness assessments, validation results, security exceptions, rollback plan, operational runbooks, forecast/unit-cost evidence, budget guardrails, and approvals.
Confirm open blockers are zero or explicitly accepted under the tailored method profile.
Record the G6 decision and decision owners.
exitCriteria: Review release evidence and go/no-go criteria evidence is recorded
validationRules: Go/no-go is evidence-based and not inferred from task completion
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Review release evidence and go/no-go criteria decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Deploy and validate progressively
taskDefinitions.purpose: Deploy and validate progressively
steps: Deploy the exact candidate to the approved environment sequence.
Run smoke, functional, security, data, observability, cost-signal, and compatibility checks.
Compare observed outcomes with release acceptance signals and stop or roll back on threshold breach.
exitCriteria: Deploy and validate progressively evidence is recorded
validationRules: Promotion evidence identifies candidate, environment, timestamp, operator, and observed result
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Deploy and validate progressively decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Complete handover and rollback rehearsal
taskDefinitions.purpose: Complete handover and rollback rehearsal
steps: Verify dashboards, alerts, runbooks, escalation paths, support ownership, cost/anomaly views, and recovery access.
Confirm rollback and data-recovery actions are usable for the release.
Accept operational ownership or return the release to rework.
exitCriteria: Complete handover and rollback rehearsal evidence is recorded
validationRules: Operational acceptance names an accountable service owner and recovery evidence
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Complete handover and rollback rehearsal decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Review release outcome and update roadmap
taskDefinitions.purpose: Review release outcome and update roadmap
steps: Compare product, operational, and unit-cost outcomes with the release hypothesis.
Accept outcomes, revise priorities, and create follow-up increments for gaps.
Record decisions and changes to scope, measures, estimates, and assumptions.
exitCriteria: Review release outcome and update roadmap evidence is recorded
validationRules: Outcome learning changes a backlog, product decision, cost forecast, or explicitly confirms the hypothesis
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Review release outcome and update roadmap decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Approve retirement scope and plan
taskDefinitions.purpose: Approve retirement scope and plan
steps: Confirm business, technical, legal, security, financial, records, and operational reasons for retirement.
Define replacement, user communication, compatibility, rollback, retention/export/deletion, and exit criteria.
Assign owners and schedule decision checkpoints.
exitCriteria: Approve retirement scope and plan evidence is recorded
validationRules: The plan identifies affected stakeholders, dependencies, records obligations, and irreversible actions
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Approve retirement scope and plan decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Execute migration and data disposition
taskDefinitions.purpose: Execute migration and data disposition
steps: Execute migration, archival, retention, deletion, or export according to approved policy.
Validate completeness, confidentiality, integrity, and recoverability where required.
Record final data and integration evidence.
exitCriteria: Execute migration and data disposition evidence is recorded
validationRules: No data or integration is silently abandoned
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Execute migration and data disposition decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Decommission service, access, and cost surfaces
taskDefinitions.purpose: Decommission service, access, and cost surfaces
steps: Continue required operational coverage during migration, then disable traffic, scheduled work, credentials, access paths, alerts, and environments in the approved order.
Verify replacement ownership, customer communication, billing cessation, and removal of residual chargeable resources.
Retain required source, model, trace, release, incident, and decision records.
exitCriteria: Decommission service, access, and cost surfaces evidence is recorded
validationRules: Decommission evidence covers runtime, data, access, cost, and support surfaces
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Decommission service, access, and cost surfaces decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Verify records retention and data disposition
taskDefinitions.purpose: Verify records retention and data disposition
steps: Reconcile every declared data class, store, backup, export, legal hold, record series, and derived copy with the approved disposition.
Verify deletion, sanitization, transfer, retention ownership, and evidence custody with Security and Service Owners.
Record unresolved obligations as blockers to G8 rather than closing them by exception without authority.
exitCriteria: Verify records retention and data disposition evidence is recorded
validationRules: Every governed data set has disposition evidence and a custodian
G8 is blocked by an unowned retention, deletion, or legal-hold obligation
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Verify records retention and data disposition decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Complete closure review
taskDefinitions.purpose: Complete closure review
steps: Confirm retirement exit criteria, financial closure, records, and custodians are complete.
Evaluate Development and Delivery evidence together with operational shutdown evidence at shared G8; do not model this synchronization as an activity-flow edge between the processes.
Review product, architecture, operational, economic, and process outcomes.
Publish reusable patterns, risks, and process changes for future projects.
exitCriteria: Complete closure review evidence is recorded
validationRules: Closure identifies retained evidence, unresolved obligations, and accountable custodians
G8 is accepted only when no live release remains and cost, access, and data obligations are closed
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Complete closure review decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Review SLOs, telemetry, cost, and product outcomes
taskDefinitions.purpose: Review SLOs, telemetry, cost, and product outcomes
steps: Inspect service levels, errors, cost, security signals, usage, provider events, and product outcome measures.
Compare observations with the service, product, forecast, budget, and unit-cost hypotheses.
Capture actionable demand as visible service work items rather than inserting hidden work into a release plan.
exitCriteria: Review SLOs, telemetry, cost, and product outcomes evidence is recorded
validationRules: Operational decisions are based on identified evidence and thresholds
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Review SLOs, telemetry, cost, and product outcomes decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Triage and make service demand ready
taskDefinitions.purpose: Triage and make service demand ready
steps: Record the demand source, impact, affected service, evidence, owner, and requested outcome on the Kanban board.

Where the item is maintenance, classify its purpose as corrective, preventive, adaptive, additive, or perfective; record any emergency temporary-restoration status; assign a class of service separately according to the board policy.
Refine the item until it meets the Ready policy and identify its likely disposition: operations-only response, the shortest safe model-driven change path, or a planned release backlog.
exitCriteria: Triage and make service demand ready evidence is recorded
validationRules: Maintenance purpose, emergency-temporary status, and class of service are recorded independently
Every ready item has an accountable owner, expected outcome, evidence need, and visible disposition
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Triage and make service demand ready decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Replenish, pull, and manage Kanban flow
taskDefinitions.purpose: Replenish, pull, and manage Kanban flow
steps: At the replenishment cadence, select eligible items into Ready according to capacity, risk, class-of-service policy, and value; pull a ready item only when the downstream WIP control permits.

Use the board to manage work-item age, blocked work, service-level expectations, and reserved service capacity; an expedite item may displace other work only under the explicit expedite policy and must remain visible.

Hold a daily flow review and periodic service-delivery review using WIP, throughput, cycle time, work-item age, SLE attainment, arrival rate, blocked time, and expedite frequency; adapt the Definition of Workflow through an explicit improvement decision.
exitCriteria: Replenish, pull, and manage Kanban flow evidence is recorded
validationRules: A team does not start ordinary service work beyond its WIP control
The expedite class has at most one active item unless the method profile records an exceptional incident-command policy
Requested, Ready, In Progress, Verify, and Done states and their entry/exit policies are visible on the board
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Replenish, pull, and manage Kanban flow decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Manage incidents and emergency recovery
taskDefinitions.purpose: Manage incidents and emergency recovery
steps: Triage impact, stabilize service, communicate status, and execute approved recovery actions.
Record incident timeline, affected scope, decisions, temporary modifications, and evidence.
Create permanent corrective, security, or change work for systemic causes and keep it visible after restoration.
exitCriteria: Manage incidents and emergency recovery evidence is recorded
validationRules: Recovery and customer impact are recorded before closure
An emergency temporary modification is not treated as the permanent corrective change
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Manage incidents and emergency recovery decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Perform problem and risk learning
taskDefinitions.purpose: Perform problem and risk learning
steps: Analyze contributing causes across requirements, models, transformation, generation, deployment, and operation.
Update controls, tests, model patterns, risk treatment, process guidance, or method profile as appropriate.
Place permanent corrective work on the Kanban board or deliberately commit it to a planned release, and verify reconciliation after any emergency downstream fix.
exitCriteria: Perform problem and risk learning evidence is recorded
validationRules: The corrective action is routed to the earliest responsible source rather than only patched downstream
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Perform problem and risk learning decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Assess and route a maintenance change
taskDefinitions.purpose: Assess and route a maintenance change
steps: Classify the authoritative source as product/domain, architecture, platform, generator, artifact, or operations and confirm whether the item remains a bounded Kanban service item or is committed to a planned release.
Use traces and dependency ownership to identify impacted downstream levels and teams.

Send product-changing work to the Development and Delivery Process at the smallest affected phase or activity; after release, reconcile emergency downstream fixes into the authoritative source and close the service item only when evidence returns.
exitCriteria: Assess and route a maintenance change evidence is recorded
validationRules: The change record identifies source revision, impacted levels, downstream evidence, acceptance decision, and service-work-item disposition
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Assess and route a maintenance change decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Inspect flow, quality, cost, and coordination metrics
taskDefinitions.purpose: Inspect flow, quality, cost, and coordination metrics
steps: Review planned-delivery forecast, Kanban WIP, throughput, cycle time, work-item age, SLE attainment, demand arrival rate, expedite frequency, rework, trace coverage, blockers, dependency age, escaped defects, cost/unit trends, and product outcomes.
Look for systemic queues, starvation between planned and service work, missing work products, invalid gates, and coordination failures.
Approve bounded changes to the Definition of Workflow, capacity policy, DevOps interface, cost guardrails, or method profile and record their expected effect.
exitCriteria: Inspect flow, quality, cost, and coordination metrics evidence is recorded
validationRules: Metrics lead to inspectable improvement experiments rather than individual performance rankings
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Inspect flow, quality, cost, and coordination metrics decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

workProductDefinitions.name: Product and System Charter
workProductDefinitions.description: Product goal, outcome hypothesis, scope boundaries, constraints, and success measures.

workProductDefinitions.name: Feasibility and Serverless Suitability Record
workProductDefinitions.description: Compared alternatives, workload fit, assumptions, experiments, provider decision, and recommendation.

workProductDefinitions.name: Cost Model and Budget Guardrails
workProductDefinitions.description: Demand drivers, scenario ranges, allocation tags, unit economics, budgets, anomaly thresholds, confidence, and review cadence.

workProductDefinitions.name: Risk and Opportunity Register
workProductDefinitions.description: Cause-event-effect statements, exposure, owner, treatment, trigger, review date, and evidence.

workProductDefinitions.name: Situational Method Profile
workProductDefinitions.description: Tailored lifecycle, roles, work products, gates, evidence rules, and metrics for the project context.

workProductDefinitions.name: Team Topology and Dependency Map
workProductDefinitions.description: Team ownership, interfaces, dependency board, decision rights, and coordination cadence.

workProductDefinitions.name: Increment and Integrated Plan Record
workProductDefinitions.description: Roadmap/release hypothesis, slice goal, scope, acceptance evidence, model revisions, transformation runs, forecast, and retrospective results.

workProductDefinitions.name: Release, Recovery, Handover and Promotion Record
workProductDefinitions.description: Immutable candidate, exact model/artifact revisions, recovery plan, readiness/handover pack, approvals, deployment evidence, rollback identity, and outcome.

workProductDefinitions.name: Operational Evidence, Incident and Change Record
workProductDefinitions.description: SLOs, incidents/problems, changes, capacity, cost, security, provider events, product outcomes, and learning.

workProductDefinitions.name: Retrospective and Improvement Record
workProductDefinitions.description: Observed outcomes, process/model friction, measures, decisions, owners, experiments, reusable candidates, and no-op rationale.

workProductDefinitions.name: Service Work Item
workProductDefinitions.description: A production, maintenance, service, or improvement demand item with source, maintenance purpose where applicable, emergency-temporary status, class of service, severity, owner, service-level expectation, state, age, evidence, and disposition.

workProductDefinitions.name: Kanban Service-Delivery Policy and Board
workProductDefinitions.description: The explicit Definition of Workflow and visible Kanban board: requested/ready/started/finished points, workflow states, WIP controls, classes of service, service-level expectations, replenishment and review cadences, capacity policy, and flow metrics.

workProductDefinitions.name: Retirement, Data-Disposition and Closure Record
workProductDefinitions.description: Retirement decision, migration, retention/export/deletion evidence, decommission evidence, financial closure, and retained knowledge.

guidance.name: Thin vertical increments
guidance.text: Deliver one capability slice through CIM → PIM → PSM → artifact readiness per engine revolution. The engine repeats inside release, operations, and retirement lifecycle governance; avoid big-bang modeling.

guidance.name: Human-in-the-loop transforms
guidance.text: ETL and M2T are assistive. ManualDecision and readiness gates block promotion when automation is uncertain.

guidance.name: Empirical process control
guidance.text: Plan a small vertical slice, inspect executable model evidence at each gate, and adapt the backlog after artifact review.

sourceOfTruth: The project work tracker stores one process-run record per increment or release candidate.
The model repository stores the model revision, transformation run, validation evidence, and readiness assessment.
The release record stores the exact accepted model, generator, artifact, test, and deployment revisions.

aggregation.rule: Aggregate by increment, team, release, and product; never average away a blocking finding.
aggregation.teamCoordination: Publish a shared dependency board with ownership, dependency type, due date, and escalation path.
aggregation.reviewCadence: Daily local coordination, per-increment review/retrospective, and per-release readiness review.

metrics.name: Eligible task completion
metrics.cadence: each workday and at gate review
metrics.interpretation: Visibility only; never substitute for a usable increment.

metrics.name: Increment flow time
metrics.interpretation: Use trends to tune slice size and expose queues.

metrics.name: Rework rate
metrics.formula: reopened tasks caused by a finding / completed tasks
metrics.interpretation: Inspect causes; do not use as an individual performance score.

metrics.name: Trace coverage
metrics.formula: accepted scope items with source-to-evidence trace / accepted scope items
metrics.cadence: at every level gate and release
metrics.interpretation: A low value blocks confidence even when task completion is high.

metrics.name: Open blocking findings
metrics.interpretation: Must be zero or covered by an explicit, time-bound risk acceptance.

metrics.name: Manual decision closure
metrics.formula: accepted/rejected/waived manual decisions / blocking manual decisions
metrics.interpretation: Open decisions remain visible and are not silently treated as done.

metrics.name: Accepted vertical-slice rate
metrics.interpretation: A slice is accepted only when it is usable and all required evidence exists.

metrics.name: Cross-team dependency age
metrics.formula: now - openedAt for the oldest unresolved dependency
metrics.interpretation: Escalate aging dependencies before they become integration surprises.

metrics.name: Release frequency
metrics.interpretation: Interpret with change failure rate, recovery time, and product outcomes.

metrics.name: Gate decision time
metrics.source: gate decision records and evidence-ready events
metrics.cadence: at G0-G8 and per repeated G2-G7 decision
metrics.interpretation: Expose assurance queues and missing decision authority; never optimize by weakening required evidence.

metrics.name: Cost forecast variance
metrics.formula: (observed cost - forecast cost) / forecast cost for the same demand interval
metrics.source: cost model, allocation tags, workload telemetry, and billing evidence
metrics.interpretation: Recalibrate workload assumptions and unit economics; a variance is a learning signal, not automatically a failure.

metrics.name: Open closure obligations
metrics.formula: count(open live releases, access paths, retained-data duties, legal holds, chargeable resources, and support obligations)
metrics.source: retirement record, operational evidence, records register, access inventory, and cost evidence
metrics.cadence: during Phase 2 and mandatory at G8
metrics.interpretation: Must reach zero before G8 unless an obligation is transferred to a named custodian under an accepted policy.

governance.gate: The end-to-end development process coordinates its level-specific processes; it does not waive any level gate or the artifact/release process.

processEngine.description: One vertical CIM → PIM → PSM → artifact-readiness revolution per capability increment, embedded in release, operations, and retirement governance.

deliverable.name: Deployable increment
deliverable.description: Accepted models at all levels, generated artifacts, verification evidence, and an explicit increment decision for one slice.

loop.guidance: After increment acceptance, either start the next capability slice or leave the engine for release assembly. Any downstream finding re-enters the smallest affected child process through the recorded change workflow.

releaseCycle.name: Continuous Delivery Release Cycle
releaseCycle.guidance: Repeat delivery Activities—not Phases—for each selected release inside the single Active Product Construction and Evolution Phase. Operations and Maintenance independently sustains accepted live baselines.

serviceDeliveryFlow.name: Continuous Kanban Service-Delivery and Maintenance System
serviceDeliveryFlow.guidance: Production, maintenance, and improvement demand is visualized on the service Kanban board, made ready through explicit policies, and pulled only within WIP controls. Operations-only work may complete in this system; bounded product changes use the shortest safe MDE path and applicable release controls; broader changes are deliberately committed to a planned release.

lifecycleTransitions.guidance: Begin planned delivery only after the method profile, ownership, controls, and first increment hypothesis are accepted.

At G7, the promoted release becomes an accepted live baseline owned by the Operations and Maintenance Process. This starts that ongoing process for the first release and updates its live-release set for later releases.

Route product-changing maintenance to the earliest authoritative Development and Delivery activity. Operations continues for the accepted baseline while the change is engineered, qualified, released, and returned with evidence.
Retain the last accepted operating baseline and return corrective work to the earliest affected delivery activity before requalification.
Start the next planned release from roadmap demand or service work deliberately committed to planned delivery; Operations and Maintenance continues for all accepted live baselines.
Begin the sequential Retirement phase only after retirement is authorized and in-flight development/release work is resolved or explicitly transferred.

reworkLoops.name: PIM Discovery Feedback to CIM
reworkLoops.trigger: PIM refinement reveals missing CIM concepts for the increment.
reworkLoops.guidance: Extend CIM via change workflow; re-run CIM EVL before re-transform.

reworkLoops.name: PSM Platform Feedback to PIM
reworkLoops.trigger: AWS constraints require PIM architecture changes.
reworkLoops.guidance: Adjust PIM policies or integration; re-run PIM→PSM ETL.

reworkLoops.name: M2T Artifact Feedback to PSM
reworkLoops.trigger: Generated artifacts fail validation or deployment dry-run.
reworkLoops.guidance: Fix PSM at source stage; regenerate artifacts.

processEngine.spemMapping: MODRISS extension realized as an Activity(kind = Iteration) containing process Activities and WorkSequences.

phases.name: Inception, Tailoring & Organization
phases.objective: Establish the product/system purpose, process profile, team topology, quality baseline, and release strategy before modeling begins.
entryCriteria: A problem, opportunity, or mandated change has an accountable sponsor
exitCriteria: The method profile is approved
Teams, ownership, dependencies, and decision rights are explicit
The first increment has a testable outcome hypothesis
phases.tailoringNote: Tailor by risk, novelty, regulatory exposure, team distribution, and architecture volatility; retain evidence and gate obligations even when activities are combined.

stages.name: Product and System Intent
stages.objective: Turn the opportunity into an outcome-oriented product/system charter and release hypothesis.

stages.name: Feasibility, Serverless Suitability & Economic Viability
stages.objective: Compare solution alternatives and make the G0 investment decision before committing the method and architecture.

stages.name: Situational Process Tailoring
stages.objective: Select and tailor reusable method content and process activities to the project context without removing essential control objectives.

stages.name: Team Topology & Coordination
stages.objective: Make ownership and coordination explicit for multiple teams working on one integrated model and product.

stages.name: Quality, Security & Operations Baseline
stages.objective: Set cross-cutting quality, security, operational, and release constraints before design detail accumulates.

phases.name: Active Product Construction & Evolution
phases.objective: Construct and evolve the product through repeatable model-driven increments and releases while the independent Operations and Maintenance Process sustains accepted live baselines.
entryCriteria: G1 authorizes the product, method profile, team topology, and first delivery hypothesis
exitCriteria: Retirement is authorized and no development or release work remains in flight
phases.tailoringNote: This Phase occurs once. Repeatable delivery iterations and release activities run inside it; they are not phases.

stages.name: Frame Increment
stages.objective: Select a thin, valuable, testable capability slice and establish its evidence plan.

stages.name: CIM Child Process
stages.objective: Refine business intent and domain behavior for the selected slice.

iterationLoops.name: PIM Discovery Feedback to CIM
iterationLoops.trigger: PIM refinement reveals missing CIM concepts for the increment.
iterationLoops.guidance: Extend CIM via change workflow; re-run CIM EVL before re-transform.

stages.name: CIM → PIM Transformation
stages.objective: Transform the accepted CIM revision into PIM scaffolding while preserving traceability and surfacing manual decisions.

stages.name: PIM Child Process
stages.objective: Refine service boundaries, contracts, data, behavior, integration, assurance, and platform intent.

iterationLoops.name: PIM Discovery Feedback to CIM
iterationLoops.trigger: PIM refinement reveals missing CIM concepts for the increment.
iterationLoops.guidance: Extend CIM via change workflow; re-run CIM EVL before re-transform.

iterationLoops.name: PSM Platform Feedback to PIM
iterationLoops.trigger: AWS constraints require PIM architecture changes.
iterationLoops.guidance: Adjust PIM policies or integration; re-run PIM→PSM ETL.

stages.name: PIM → AWS PSM Transformation
stages.objective: Map accepted platform-independent architecture to AWS-specific deployment intent.

stages.name: PSM Child Process
stages.objective: Refine AWS resources, relationships, security, observability, and deployment readiness for the slice.

iterationLoops.name: PSM Platform Feedback to PIM
iterationLoops.trigger: AWS constraints require PIM architecture changes.
iterationLoops.guidance: Adjust PIM policies or integration; re-run PIM→PSM ETL.

iterationLoops.name: M2T Artifact Feedback to PSM
iterationLoops.trigger: Generated artifacts fail validation or deployment dry-run.
iterationLoops.guidance: Fix PSM at source stage; regenerate artifacts.

stages.name: Model-to-Text Generation
stages.objective: Generate a reproducible artifact baseline from the accepted PSM revision.

stages.name: Increment Readiness & Acceptance
stages.objective: Verify the exact generated candidate, capture acceptance evidence, and decide whether the increment is usable, reworkable, or deferred.

iterationLoops.name: M2T Artifact Feedback to PSM
iterationLoops.trigger: Generated artifacts fail validation or deployment dry-run.
iterationLoops.guidance: Fix PSM at source stage; regenerate artifacts.

stages.name: Release Train Assembly
stages.objective: Compose and verify a release from accepted increment records.

stages.name: Progressive Promotion
stages.objective: Promote the release through environments with controlled observation and rollback readiness.

stages.name: Release Review
stages.objective: Inspect release outcomes and feed product, process, and architecture learning back into the backlog.

phases.name: Retire, Migrate & Close
phases.objective: Retire a product or service safely, preserve required knowledge and evidence, and close the lifecycle with explicit learning.
entryCriteria: Replacement, migration, or end-of-life obligations are known
exitCriteria: Users, data, integrations, environments, and operational ownership are safely transitioned or closed
Required records and lessons are retained
Shared G8 closure evidence is accepted and no live release remains

stages.name: Retirement Decision & Plan
stages.objective: Define why, when, and how the service will be retired while operations continue safely.

stages.name: Migrate and Decommission
stages.objective: Move or dispose of data, users, integrations, infrastructure, and operational obligations safely.

stages.name: Closure & Organizational Learning
stages.objective: Assemble Development and Delivery closure evidence, evaluate it with Operations and Maintenance evidence at shared G8, and feed reusable learning into future method profiles and product planning.

processComponents.name: Operations and Maintenance Process
processComponents.objective: Operate the service and manage production, maintenance, and improvement demand through a continuous Kanban service-delivery system while planned releases continue through the increment engine; restore service, reconcile authoritative sources, and learn.
entryCriteria: G7 operational handover has accepted at least one live release
exitCriteria: G8 lifecycle closure is accepted and no live release remains

activities.name: Operate and Observe
activities.objective: Use operational evidence to assess service health, user outcomes, and control effectiveness.

activities.name: Kanban Service-Delivery Management
activities.objective: Visualize and manage service demand through an explicit Definition of Workflow, replenishment, pull, WIP controls, service expectations, and feedback cadences.

activities.name: Incident, Problem & Risk Response
activities.objective: Restore service and address systemic causes while preserving traceability and learning.

activities.name: Maintenance Change and Reconciliation
activities.objective: Evolve the product through controlled impact analysis, authoritative-source change, release, and emergency-fix reconciliation.

activities.name: Service and Process Improvement
activities.objective: Improve the product and both connected processes using evidence from releases, service work, incidents, and dependencies.

workflows.name: Cross-Level Change Propagation
workflows.trigger: A model change at any level must propagate through CIM → PIM → PSM → artifacts.
steps: Complete level-local change workflow and EVL gate for the source level.
Run Impact Analysis on TraceModel: list downstream TraceLinks with reduced confidence.
Re-run ETL for affected level pair (cim-to-pim, pim-to-awspsm) with merge strategy.
Replay refinement phases on target level for impacted increment slice only.
Regenerate M2T artifacts; run end-to-end validation suite.
Record ManualDecision for human resolution items; update readiness assessments.

workflows.name: Post-Transform CIM Change
workflows.trigger: CIM must change after PIM or PSM already exists for this project.
steps: Freeze downstream models or branch increment.
Apply CIM change with full impact analysis.
Re-run CIM EVL and readiness gate.
Re-execute CIM→PIM ETL; reconcile PIM trace links and manual decisions.
Propagate to PSM and artifacts per end-to-end change workflow.

workflows.name: Post-Transform PIM Change
workflows.trigger: PIM must change after PSM or artifacts exist.
steps: Apply PIM change with impact analysis on trace links to CIM and PSM.
Re-run PIM EVL and readiness.
Re-execute PIM→PSM ETL; review platform mapping deltas.
Regenerate M2T artifacts; run deployment dry-run.

workflows.name: Post-M2T PSM Change
workflows.trigger: PSM changes after artifacts were generated or deployed.
steps: Apply PSM model change at owning phase.
Re-run PSM EVL and integration views.
Regenerate M2T artifacts; diff against prior generation.
Run CI validation and staged deployment.

milestones.name: Pursue, explore, redirect, or stop
milestones.acceptanceCondition: An authorized value, feasibility, economic, and risk decision is recorded.

milestones.name: Process and organization ready
milestones.acceptanceCondition: The tailored way of working, ownership, controls, and first increment are authorized.

milestones.name: CIM accepted for the slice
milestones.acceptanceCondition: Meaning, requirements, behavior, acceptance, trace, and explicit semantic-validation evidence are adequate.

milestones.name: PIM accepted and platform-mappable
milestones.acceptanceCondition: Contracts, failure behavior, security, data, SLOs, trace, and provider capability needs are explicit.

milestones.name: PSM accepted for generation
milestones.acceptanceCondition: The exact PSM revision, trace, manual decisions, and explicit semantic-validation evidence are accepted.

milestones.name: Increment accepted, reworked, or deferred
milestones.acceptanceCondition: Value, verification, security, operability, trace, and explicit exceptions are accepted for the exact increment.

milestones.name: Release authorized, rejected, or exception accepted
milestones.acceptanceCondition: The exact immutable candidate and recovery, assurance, operational, and economic evidence are accepted.

milestones.name: Release transitioned to Operations and Maintenance
milestones.acceptanceCondition: The running release, support obligations, observability, recovery, and ownership are accepted.

milestones.name: Shared lifecycle closure accepted
milestones.acceptanceCondition: No live release, unowned data/records obligation, active access path, residual chargeable resource, or unresolved closure blocker remains.
